title: EXP-039 — Single FX_ IDO Project Creation and Recovery
objective: Determine whether the current authenticated Site Developer user can create exactly one IDO project named FX_HelloWorldProject01 using the supported Web Client IDO Projects maintenance form, save it once, close the maintenance surface, reopen it, and recover the same project definition. Before mutation, establish that Filter-in-Place works using a known-existing positive-control project and verify that FX_HelloWorldProject01 does not already exist, including case-insensitive collisions. Observe and record the Project Name, Description, Access As, naming rules, creation permissions, Save outcome, and post-reopen values. Stop before mutation if the project name is unavailable, the query cannot be verified, a mandatory prefix is incompatible, or any required control is unavailable. Stop on the first creation or Save failure without retrying. Do not create an IDO, SQL table, Form, or application data record.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, the EXP-038 experiment record, evidence/EXP-038/t1-evidence-index.md, and the relevant local IDO development documentation before browser mutation.
Inspect the authenticated Web Client and verify the intended DEM configuration and usable IDO Projects maintenance UI. Record visibly available role or permission information.
Use Web Client > Select Form > IdoProjects, or inspect the existing IDO Projects instance inherited from EXP-038.
Inspect inherited unsaved Filter-in-Place criteria. Clear or dismiss criteria using supported controls without saving or modifying existing project records.
The inherited Sql Tables maintenance tab may be closed only if visibly clean and without saving.
Inspect the rendered Project Name, Description, Access As, toolbar New, Save, Filter-in-Place, and ordinary close controls.
Execute one positive-control Filter-in-Place query using a known-existing project identified from the visible inventory. Require a returned row showing the expected Project Name.

Using the verified query mechanism, search for FX_HelloWorldProject01 and establish zero existing case-insensitive collisions through supported visible evidence. Do not rely on an unverified empty result or undocumented wildcard behavior.
Inspect any visible enforced object prefix, naming restriction, or pre-filled Access As value before committing. Stop if the required project name cannot be used unchanged.
After every preflight gate passes, use the supported toolbar New action once to begin one experimental project record.
Enter Project Name exactly FX_HelloWorldProject01 and Description exactly Factory Hello World test project.
Leave Access As and all other optional fields at supported defaults unless documented requirements establish an appropriate value. Never invent or override an Access As identifier.
If the UI rejects FX_HelloWorldProject01 because of its underscore or any other naming restriction, capture the exact error and stop without choosing another name.
Commit the project through at most one supported ordinary Save attempt. Capture visible validation, success or failure messages, and available responses.
After successful Save, verify the selected project has the exact Project Name, Description, and displayed Access As. Establish that no unsaved changes or error state remain.
Close the clean IDO Projects maintenance surface once and reopen it through the supported Select Form workflow.
Query FX_HelloWorldProject01 again and compare the recovered Project Name, Description, and Access As against the post-Save baseline.
Capture decisive screenshots and accessibility snapshots under evidence/EXP-039/, clearly identifying the target project, controls, preflight results, Save outcome, and post-reopen state.
Record the exact New, Save, close, reopen, and query operation counts, recovery-budget usage, any error, and all observed side effects.
Update only the EXP-039 experiment record and evidence/EXP-039/. Preserve earlier experiments, recipes, guides, and factory configuration.
out_of_scope: Creating SQL tables, columns, triggers, indexes, database views, or application data records.
Creating or modifying IDOs, IDO properties, or IDO relationships.
Opening the New IDO wizard, New Data Maintenance wizard, or any other creation wizard.
Using the fallback name FXHelloWorld01 or any alternative project name.
Creating or modifying Mongoose Forms, components, variables, event handlers, scripts, or workflows.
Changing the membership or definitions of existing IDO projects.
Runtime CRUD testing or application integration testing.
Deployment, FormSync, synchronization, metadata-cache unloading, or regeneration.
Direct SQL execution, direct database access, internal endpoints, browser JavaScript, or unsupported APIs.
Changing security roles, authentication configuration, tenant permissions, or user preferences.
Starting EXP-040 or any unrelated experiment.
Claims about independent database durability, cache eviction, cross-session persistence, or replay verification.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values
Never create, modify, or delete any Mongoose artifact whose name does not begin with FX_.
Never create more than one IDO project.
Never use a project name other than FX_HelloWorldProject01.
Never use FXHelloWorld01 as a fallback, even if the preferred project name is rejected.
Never proceed with mutation until a supported positive-control query proves that Filter-in-Place executes successfully.
Never proceed if FX_HelloWorldProject01 already exists or its absence cannot be verified, including case-insensitive collisions.
Never proceed if an enforced prefix or naming restriction prevents the exact project name.
Never manually override Access As without explicit documented authority and separately reviewed scope.
Never press New IDO, IDOs, or any wizard-launch control associated with IDO creation.
Never create or modify an IDO, SQL table, Form, event handler, script, workflow, or application data record.
Never alter an existing project's name, description, Access As, membership, permissions, or other metadata.
Never perform more than one project New action or one Save attempt.
Never retry an uncertain Save or attempt another project creation after a failure.
Never infer successful creation solely from a click, success message, or an unsaved editor.
Never bypass disabled controls, permission errors, validation failures, or unavailable supported UI using scripts, direct URLs, hidden controls, or internal APIs.
Never deliberately sign in, reauthenticate, reset the session, or restart services during the experiment. Stop if authentication blocks the required operation.
Never perform deployment, FormSync, cache unloading, regeneration, or direct SQL execution.
Never delete experimental objects without separate operator authorization.
Never exceed one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Stop when either required recovery exceeds its allowance.
Never modify repository files outside the EXP-039 experiment record and evidence/EXP-039/.

acceptance_checks.description: Before mutation, repository evidence identifies the documented IDO project prerequisite, AGENTS.md authorization, and EXP-038 findings. Browser evidence shows the authenticated target configuration, available IDO Projects maintenance UI, visible permissions where available, and the New and Save controls. The evidence explicitly distinguishes User editing scope from potentially configuration-wide IDO project creation.

Before mutation, a supported Filter-in-Place positive-control query visibly returns a known-existing project with the expected Project Name. The same verified mechanism establishes zero exact and case-insensitive matches for FX_HelloWorldProject01. Capture query criteria, the positive-control row, and settled target-query results. Stop before mutation if the collision check remains inconclusive.

Supported pre-creation UI inspection records the available Project Name, Description, and Access As fields, their initial values, any naming restrictions, and any enforced prefix. The exact name FX_HelloWorldProject01 must remain usable. A visible naming rejection fails this check and stops the experiment without a fallback.

The supported IDO Projects UI confirms creation of exactly one project named FX_HelloWorldProject01 through one New action and at most one Save attempt. Its saved Description is exactly Factory Hello World test project. The displayed Access As value is captured. Evidence identifies the successful commit, an error-free clean state, and the absence of pending changes.

After one ordinary close and one supported reopen of the IDO Projects maintenance surface, FX_HelloWorldProject01 can be selected again. Rendered evidence identifies its Project Name, Description, and Access As, and a recorded comparison confirms all values match the post-Save baseline. The recovered surface is clean without visible errors.

A final supported project inventory or control-verified lookup identifies exactly one matching FX_HelloWorldProject01 record, with no duplicate or transformed target identity. The object audit records every experimental artifact and visible generated dependency. No unrelated creation operation was performed.

The final action audit reconciles exact New, Save, close, reopen, and filter-query counts, visible permissions, errors, recovery attempts, and unexpected side effects. If the experiment stops early, the report records the precise failed prerequisite and all operations actually performed rather than claiming completion.

The final evidence matrix maps AC-1 through AC-7 to exact screenshot, accessibility snapshot, or captured-response paths under evidence/EXP-039/. Evidence visibly identifies the project and its values rather than relying on filenames alone. Repository changes are confined to the EXP-039 record and evidence/EXP-039/. Findings are classified as observed only, with explicit limitations concerning independent database durability, cache behavior, and replay verification.

initial_instruction: Perform T1 read-only preflight for EXP-039 only. Read AGENTS.md, the EXP-038 record, evidence/EXP-038/t1-evidence-index.md, and relevant IDO project documentation. Inspect the authenticated Web Client, target configuration, and IDO Projects maintenance surface, including inherited unsaved filter state and the visibly available New, Save, Project Name, Description, and Access As controls. Establish one positive-control Filter-in-Place query returning a known-existing project, then verify that FX_HelloWorldProject01 has no exact or case-insensitive collision using supported visible UI. Record any enforced prefix, Access As display, naming rule, or permission restriction. Capture decisive screenshots and accessibility snapshots under evidence/EXP-039/ with a concise proof-and-limitations summary. Do not invoke New or Save in T1. Do not open New IDO, IDOs, or any creation wizard. Do not change any project. Stop on an inconclusive query, unavailable control, session prompt, or exhausted recovery allowance. Report exact evidence paths, verified prerequisites, unresolved points, and current browser state. Await a separate coordinator instruction before mutation.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-105122-w8zf. Rationale: EXP-038 stopped before mutation because its object-collision checks and SQL table/IDO creation path were unresolved. Infor 2026.x documentation indicates that an IDO project must exist before the New Data Maintenance wizard can associate an IDO with a new project. EXP-038 T1 already observed the IDO Projects maintenance surface. EXP-039 isolates this prerequisite by testing creation and persistence of exactly one FX_-prefixed IDO project. The previously proposed fallback FXHelloWorld01 is removed entirely because it violates the factory's mandatory FX_ artifact prefix. If FX_HelloWorldProject01 is rejected, the experiment stops without trying another name. | Operator review: exact-value and no-JavaScript guards added. Standard lessons apply (select a tab before acting on it; comboboxes take a literal value plus Enter; one action at a time). A naming rejection stops the run without a fallback name. Approved by the operator 2026-10-10 (IDO Projects and Sql Tables forms from EXP-038 still open).
